items.title: Switching Neurons On with Light
items.text:
On 5 October 2026, the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institutet awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. The prize __(1)__ a technique that has transformed neuroscience over the past two decades.

The story began not in the brain but in green algae. Hegemann and Nagel studied proteins that allow these single-celled organisms to __(2)__ to light. They showed that one such protein, channelrhodopsin, opens a channel in the cell membrane when light strikes it. Deisseroth then realized that if this protein could be placed in nerve cells, scientists would be able to control those cells with remarkable precision.

That is exactly what optogenetics does. By __(3)__ genes for light-sensitive proteins into specific neurons, researchers can switch those cells on or off with flashes of light, __(4)__ in a living animal. The method has helped scientists map the brain circuits involved in memory, fear, and addiction. __(5)__ most applications remain in the laboratory, researchers hope the technique will eventually lead to new treatments for blindness and neurological disorders.

items.explain: respond to light 對光產生反應；object to 是反對。
介系詞 By 後面接 V-ing。
even in a living animal 表示「甚至在活體動物身上」，強調難度。
前後語意轉折（多半還在實驗室，但希望未來能治療），用 Although。
